title: KV cache metadata-driven slot packing & spill controller
content:
Summary:

This note sketches a complementary approach to the existing KV cache proposals: a metadata-driven slot-packing allocator paired with a predictive spill controller. The goal is to reduce long-tail fragmentation while preserving low tail-latency for serving requests. Unlike aggressive global compaction, this design biases toward local, fast rearrangements and a probabilistic controller that decides when to spill to disk or higher-cost tiers.

Design goals and constraints:
- Low p99/p999 request latency for cache hits; avoid blocking GC/compaction on the serving path.
- Keep live memory utilization high while bounding fragmentation-induced blow-ups.
- Support heterogeneous item sizes (tokens+kv headers) and per-tenant soft quotas.
- Provide telemetry hooks for an automatic heuristic tuner (later ML-based) and safe operator overrides.
- Interoperate with existing prefix/KV caching and KV-sharding model.

Key ideas (overview):
1) Metadata-driven slot packing: instead of fixed slab bucket sizes, each allocation carries compact metadata (slot-class, occupancy-fraction, generation-id). The allocator maintains small packing windows (per-shard) that prefer placing items into partially-filled contiguous regions to minimize internal fragmentation.

2) Ephemeral micro-slablets: to avoid slow large compaction passes, we use many small slablets (4KB-64KB) grouped into fast coalescing rings. Micro-slablets are cheap to merge/coalesce in-place if adjacent and same-generation.

3) Predictive spill controller: a background controller continuously ingests fragmentation telemetry and request hotness signals and makes decisions whether to trigger local re-packing, full compaction of a shard, or spill cold ranges to a spill tier (SSD / remote cache). The controller is probabilistic to avoid synchronized global work.

4) Inline hugepage-awareness and alignment hints: allocator records instance-level hugepage footprint and uses alignment hints for long-lived allocations to reduce virtual memory fragmentation.

Memory layout and metadata format:
- Each item header (16-32 bytes) contains: key-hash (64-bit), value-length (24-bit), flags (4 bits), slot-class-id (8-bit), generation (8-bit), checksum/marker (8-bit). Keep header <= 32 bytes to limit metadata overhead.
- Slablet: contiguous region of memory backing N items. Slablet metadata: slablet-id, current-occupancy-count, free-bitmap (sparse compressed), last-touch-timestamp-sample, aggregation-hint (hot/cold), tenant-id.
- Packing window: a rotating set of 4 slablets that allocator prefers; allocator will probe these before allocating a new slablet.

Allocation strategy (fast path):
1) Hash -> shard -> concurrency stripe.
2) Attempt to place into packing-window slablet of matching slot-class-id using atomic test-and-set on free-bitmap.
3) If unsuccessful after limited probes, allocate a new micro-slablet from the slablet freelist and place item.
4) Update per-shard lightweight histograms: slot_fill_histogram, slot_eviction_count, write_churn_rate. These are approximate counters (exponentially decayed).

Packing and local reorganization (background but shard-local):
- Shard-local packer runs opportunistically when: (a) packing-window occupancy < threshold, (b) write_churn low and CPU available, (c) predicted benefit > cost (see controller heuristics).
- Packer picks candidate slablet pairs (source,dest) with complementary free maps and migrates live items using single-copy handoff: allocate slot in dest, atomically link, then free source slot. We keep the movement bounded per-run to avoid large latency spikes.

Spill controller heuristics and signals:
Inputs:
- fragmentation_ratio = (allocated_bytes - in_place_live_bytes) / allocated_bytes
- slot_fill_skew = entropy(slot_fill_histogram)
- churn_rate = recent writes per second per shard
- observed_latency_tail = recent p99/p999 for cache hits on shard
- failover_capacity = available memory headroom across cluster
Outputs / actions:
- No-op: if fragmentation_ratio < 0.12 and churn_rate > high -> avoid moving hot items.
- Local pack: if fragmentation_ratio > 0.2 and churn_rate low -> schedule local packer for shard.
- Aggressive compaction: if fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 and tail latency growing -> schedule multi-slab compaction with rate limit.
- Spill-to-tier: if memory headroom < safety-margin OR fragmentation_ratio high and items cold -> move cold ranges to spill tier and free their slablets.
- Backpressure to scheduler: if long compaction is ongoing, controller may signal request-router to favor other replicas to protect p99.

Predictive element (short-term):
- Use a simple logistic regression model fed with: slot_fill_skew, churn_rate, last-touch-decay, and request_heat (sampled hot-item fraction). Output: probability that a repacking run will reduce memory by >X within Y seconds. This is a low-cost model implemented as weighted sums and periodically retrained offline.

Telemetry and metrics to expose (minimal and high-signal):
- shard.fragmentation_ratio (gauge)
- shard.micro_slablet_count (gauge)
- shard.avg_slot_fill (gauge)
- shard.slot_fill_histogram (sketch / quantile)
- shard.migrated_bytes_per_minute (counter)
- shard.pack_runs (counter)
- shard.predicted_pack_benefit (gauge)
- tenant.soft_quota_used_pct (gauge)
- cluster.spill_rate (counter)
- sampling traces for moved items: moved_item_age_histogram, moved_item_latency_impact

Operational modes and safety:
- Default: conservative. Controller avoids compaction unless the predicted benefit is positive and churn is low.
- Aggressive debug mode: forced compactions and wider sampling windows for production experiments. Only enabled via operator flag / rollout.
- Tenant soft-limits: if tenant crosses soft limit, controller throttles tenant writes (early reject / degrade) instead of global compaction.

Integration with existing runtime components:
- Scheduler: controller publishes per-shard compaction windows; scheduler uses these when allocating CPU/GPU resources for background work to avoid competing with hot inference shards.
- Prefix/KV caching: when spill controller selects ranges for spill, it coordinates with prefix-caching layer to ensure subsequent prefix queries check the spill tier transparently.
- Observability & rollouts: pack runs emit events with a run-id so console and rollout system can correlate regressions.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Unexpected high churn after a pack run -> mitigation: pack runs commit incrementally and can be aborted; controller monitors p99 for regression and rolls back by marking dest slots as cold and copying back if needed (rare).
- Network partition during spill -> ensure idempotent spill markers and lease-based ownership for slablets; spilled keys must be retried.
- Memory accounting bug -> circuit-breaker: if global accounting diverges, fall back to simple per-tenant hard quotas and disable background work.

Experimentation plan (first 8 weeks):
Week 1-2: implement micro-slablets and packing-window allocator in a shadow shard (no live traffic). Collect baseline metrics.
Week 3-4: implement lightweight telemetry and the predictive regression model; run offline simulations on historical traces.
Week 5-6: enable conservative controller in canary cluster (10% traffic) with packer runs limited to 100KB/sec per shard. Observe tail latency, memory utilization.
Week 7-8: expand to 50% with gradual increase of allowed pack throughput; add spill-to-tier for very cold items.

Perf targets and success criteria:
- Reduce fragmentation_ratio by 30% compared to baseline for shards with >10% long-tail free slots.
- No more than 5% regression in p99 cache-hit latency during background work compared to baseline.
- Reduce overall cluster memory amplification from fragmentation by at least 10% in steady-state.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How small should micro-slablets be without incurring too much metadata overhead? (tradeoff: metadata vs compaction granularity)
- How to safely choose predictive thresholds across diverse tenants? (per-tenant vs global models)
- Cost model for packer: CPU vs expected memory reclaimed; should be continuous or discrete steps?

Next action items:
- [Asha] prototype packing-window allocator and micro-slablets (P0).
- [Miguel] instrument and publish the initial telemetry sketch (P0).
- [Priya] prepare offline dataset and simulation harness for predictive model training (P1).
- [Ethan] evaluate spill-tier write/read performance with current SSD config and propose format (P1).

Appendix: short pseudocode for fast allocation path:
function allocate(key, size):
  shard = shard_for(key)
  class = slot_class_for(size)
  for slablet in shard.packing_window[class]:
    if try_allocate_in_slablet(slablet):
       return pointer
  // fallback
  slablet = shard.alloc_new_slablet(class)
  return allocate_into(slablet, key, size)

Notes: this is intentionally sketchy — implementation must be careful about ABA on handoff and use small CAS-protected bitmaps for atomic slot claims.

This design is intended to be complementary to the other compaction/eviction proposals (global compaction, tiered pools). The emphasis here is on small, safe, local moves driven by compact metadata and a lightweight predictive controller that avoids unnecessary work while shrinking fragmentation steadily over time.
